current.section_name: General Service to Service Communication Security
current.text: Verify that TLS connections between internal services use trusted certificates. Where internally generated or self-signed certificates are used, the consuming service must be configured to only trust specific internal CAs and specific self-signed certificates.

master.text: Verify that TLS connections between internal services use trusted certificates. Where internally generated or self-signed certificates are used, the consuming service must be configured to only trust specific internal CAs and specific self-signed certificates.

predecessors.text: Verify that connections to and from the server use trusted TLS certificates. Where internally generated or self-signed certificates are used, the server must be configured to only trust specific internal CAs and specific self-signed certificates. All others should be rejected.

Verify that application components verify the authenticity of each side in a communication link to prevent person-in-the-middle attacks. For example, application components should validate TLS certificates and chains.

summaries.body:
ASVS 5.0.0 V12.3.4 is carried forward from 4.0.3 V9.2.1 and covers V1.9.2. V9.2.1 required trusted TLS certificates on connections to and from the server, and that internally generated or self-signed certificates be limited to specific internal CAs and specific self-signed certificates, with all others rejected. V1.9.2 required components to verify authenticity of each side in a communication link to prevent person-in-the-middle attacks, for example by validating TLS certificates and chains. The mapping records MODIFIED, moved from v4.0.3-9.2.1, covers v4.0.3-1.9.2.

On 2019-02-25 securitybits asked in #550 to change “person-In-the-middle” to “man-in-the-middle.” tghosth replied that person-in-the-middle was preferable and fixed only the capital I. On 2021-04-01 tghosth committed “Resolves #662” on V9.2.1. Mapping and those predecessors are the reliable origin. Issue #726 (moving then-V12.3.4 RFD into file download) is the old Files chapter.

The 5.0 text scopes trusted certificates to TLS connections between internal services, and says the consuming service must trust only specific internal CAs and specific self-signed certificates. V9.2.1 had spoken of connections to and from the server. On 2022-02-11 elarlang updated the communications chapter holding V9.2.1. The mapping labels the 5.0 wording MODIFIED.

Capitalisation on old V12.3.4 and the #726 RFD move are files-chapter events and did not rewrite this control.

terminology.statement: On V1.9.2, tghosth kept “person in the middle” rather than “man-in-the-middle,” treating the former as preferable; only the capital I in “In” was treated as a defect.
